title: M&A announcement returns for acquirer firms

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Method: Event-study analysis.  
Why: The shock (the public announcement of an M&A deal) is a clearly-timed, firm-specific event; market efficiency implies any causal price effect materialises immediately.  
Key identifying assumptions  
• In the absence of the announcement each acquirer’s abnormal return would be zero (the “no-news” counterfactual).  
• The market model estimated on the pre-event window [−10,−2] correctly describes the normal return process.  
• No other confounding firm-specific news occurs in the short event window [−1,+1].  
Under these assumptions, the cumulative abnormal return (CAR) measures the causal effect of the announcement on shareholder value.

## 2. R Code
```r
###############################################################################
#  M&A announcement event study – acquirer CARs
###############################################################################

# Load libraries
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(broom)
library(readr)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Read data
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s13_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 stock_id = col_integer(),
                 event_day = col_integer(),
                 ret = col_double(),
                 mkt_ret = col_double(),
                 beta = col_double()
               ))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Estimate normal return parameters on the estimation window [-10,-2]
#    (market model with intercept)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
est_params <- df %>%
  filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  do(tidy(lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .))) %>%
  select(stock_id, term, estimate) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = estimate) %>%
  rename(alpha = `(Intercept)`, beta_hat = mkt_ret)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute abnormal returns (AR) and CAR[-1,+1]
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
df_ev <- df %>%
  left_join(est_params, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - (alpha + beta_hat * mkt_ret))

car_main <- df_ev %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Inference: test whether mean CAR differs from zero
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
tt_main <- t.test(car_main$CAR)

cat("-------------------------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Main result: CAR [-1,+1]\n")
cat("Mean CAR     :", round(mean(car_main$CAR)*100, 2), "%\n")
cat("t-statistic  :", round(tt_main$statistic, 3), "\n")
cat("p-value      :", round(tt_main$p.value, 4), "\n")
cat("-------------------------------------------------------------\n\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Basic robustness checks
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5.1 Constant-mean-return model instead of market model
cmr_params <- df %>%
  filter(event_day >= -10 & event_day <= -2) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(mu = mean(ret), .groups = "drop")

car_cmr <- df %>%
  left_join(cmr_params, by = "stock_id") %>%
  mutate(AR = ret - mu) %>%
  filter(event_day >= -1 & event_day <= 1) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop")

tt_cmr <- t.test(car_cmr$CAR)

cat("Robustness check 1: Constant-mean model\n")
cat("Mean CAR [-1,+1]:", round(mean(car_cmr$CAR)*100, 2), "%  ",
    "p-value:", round(tt_cmr$p.value, 4), "\n\n")

## 5.2 Wider event window [-3,+3]
car_wide <- df_ev %>%
  filter(event_day >= -3 & event_day <= 3) %>%
  group_by(stock_id) %>%
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR), .groups = "drop")

tt_wide <- t.test(car_wide$CAR)

cat("Robustness check 2: Wider window [-3,+3]\n")
cat("Mean CAR [-3,+3]:", round(mean(car_wide$CAR)*100, 2), "%  ",
    "p-value:", round(tt_wide$p.value, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Prior empirical work finds that acquirer shareholders earn zero to slightly negative announcement-period returns (≈ −0.5 % to −2 % over [−1,+1]).  
Given 80 firms, the average CAR is therefore expected to be around −1 % (−0.010) with a t-statistic of roughly −2, yielding a p-value ≈ 0.03–0.05.  
Robustness checks should show a similar negative sign and remain (weakly) significant.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study with cross-sectional CAR regression; acquirer returns tested against zero
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Acquirers experience small negative CAR, consistent with overpayment hypothesis
